key_insight: A dual-resonator silver microcavity can simultaneously boost triplet sensitizer absorption and direct upconverted emission, overcoming the usual tradeoff in solid-state triplet-triplet annihilation upconversion.
engineering_relevance: This approach could make low-intensity sub-bandgap photon harvesting more practical for photovoltaic and other optoelectronic devices by increasing usable emission without requiring higher sensitizer loading.
method: Thermally co-evaporated a rubrene:palladium phthalocyanine active layer inside a planar silver microcavity.
Aligned one dispersive cavity mode with the PdPC absorption peak at 32° to enhance sensitizer absorption.
Used a second cavity mode to directionally out-couple upconverted emission while managing reabsorption losses.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a 12-fold absorptance increase at 665 nm, a 22-fold peak increase in detected upconversion emission, and a 4.5-fold enhancement when integrated over emission.
watch_item: Microcavity benefits may depend on precise angle/mode alignment, and reabsorption plus aggregation-quenching constraints still limit practical device optimization.
paper_title: Dual-Resonator Organic Microcavities for Triplet-Triplet Annihilation Upconversion
